overview: Tuvalu is one of the smallest countries in the world, made up of nine small islands in the central Pacific. Its capital is Funafuti. Tuvalu became independent from the United Kingdom in 1978. It earns money from fishing licences and from its internet domain name, .tv.

geography.text: All of Tuvalu's islands are low coral atolls or reef islands, with the highest land only a few metres above sea level. This makes it one of the countries most threatened by rising seas. There are no rivers, so people depend on collecting rainwater.

history.text: Tuvalu was settled by Polynesians. As the Ellice Islands, it was run by Britain together with the Gilbert Islands, today Kiribati. In 1974 the Ellice Islanders voted to separate, and Tuvalu became independent in 1978. In 2023 it signed a treaty with Australia offering residency to Tuvaluans threatened by climate change.

events.title: British protectorate
events.text: Britain takes control of the Ellice and Gilbert Islands.

events.title: Vote to separate
events.text: The Ellice Islands vote to split from the Gilberts.

events.title: Joins the UN
events.text: Tuvalu becomes a member of the United Nations.

events.title: Treaty with Australia
events.text: Australia offers Tuvaluans a way to move there as seas rise.
